issues.legal_issue: When a land-grant agreement provides for reversion upon a company's winding up, the reversion transfers title to the grantor and does not preserve an independent right of possession in the company.
material_facts: The agreement provided that the land would revert to the State if the company was wound up.
The company was ordered to be wound up.
The company had not operated the factory, and the State claimed possession of the land.
issues.conclusion: Title to the land vested in the State upon the winding-up order, and the agreement did not entitle the company to remain in possession after title vested.
issues.legal_principle: Under the third proviso to clause 6(a) of the agreement, land reverted to the State upon winding up. The fourth proviso addressed delivery of possession and the removal of machinery and structures; it did not preserve a right to possess the land after title had vested in the State. The Court relied on the terms of the agreement and cited no earlier cases or statutory provisions.

predicates.civil_appeal_over_contractual_land_posse: The matter comes before the court on appeal in a dispute over possession of land governed by an agreement.
predicates.land_grant_agreement_provides_reversion_: The agreement granting land provides that the land reverts to the grantor if the company is wound up.
predicates.company_is_ordered_wound_up: A court orders the company to be wound up.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns contractual land possession, the agreement provides for reversion on winding up, and the company is ordered wound up, the land title reverts without a continuing company possession right.

issues.legal_issue: A written removal notice sent by a state official to a company's provisional liquidators can satisfy the contractual notice requirement for removal of property from land that has reverted to the State.
material_facts: After provisional liquidators were appointed, the Director of Industries sent them a written notice requiring removal of property from the land.
The company was later ordered to be wound up, triggering the agreement's land-reversion provision.
The machinery was auctioned and valuable property had been removed; only a temporary structure and grass remained on the land.
The notice period had expired when the State sought possession.
issues.conclusion: The notice satisfied the fourth proviso to clause 6(a), and the State was entitled to possession after the notice period; the Court directed that possession be handed over within a further six months.
issues.legal_principle: The fourth proviso to clause 6(a) required written notice to remove machinery, structures, and other property, and provided for their vesting in the State if they were not removed within the specified period. On the circumstances before it, the Court held that the written notice sent to the provisional liquidators satisfied that requirement. It relied on the agreement and cited no earlier cases or statutory provisions.
